Circumstance has set up this trade as one of the best I'll ever be a part of.

WDC is Western Digital which recently acquired SanDisk SNDK, and their combined financials should speak for themselves http://www.gurufocus.com/financials/WDC http://www.gurufocus.com/financials/SNDK

The collapse in this sector's financials and stock prices should be self-explanatory, but STX still an HDD-only company rebounding in the stock market while WDC remains drastically undervalued and flat despite buying into 1/5 of the SSD market makes less sense.

It all becomes clear as mud when looking at WDC's latest financials. Interest expense looks to be around $800 million per year as of the latest quarterly data. At the last quarter's rate of income, it looks like the world could come to an end.

Management recently announced they had already reduced that by $125 million annually, making the annual burden a joke relative to the expected combined incomes and cash of the new WDC based upon the next years' estimates. It is now in the second quarter of a rebound in business. Revenue will be about 30% higher than the same quarter last year, and if HPQ's comments about parts shortages are true, revenue should continue rebounding at a high rate.

The overreaction is so strong that the combined WDC company is now trading for $10 billion while pre-acquisition, they were trading at almost $30 billion. A triple that doesn't even include future growth is my kind of margin of safety.

The opportunity is magnified by the current state of WDC's options. Shorts have returned to the stock, and the equally strong market opinion on both sides has flattened out the implied volatility to 40%. Aside from the drop after earnings, the stock has had flat trading days. This makes options on WDC extremely cheap, providing an even larger margin of safety so long as the options are longed not shorted.

Full disclosure: I own WDC straps and am going to buy more.
